summary: Set AI risk, procurement and oversight controls for public services. Explore practical governance tools and enrol in the five-day course.
lede: AI governance sets decision rights, controls and review practices for AI use in public services and regulatory work. For policy advisers, digital-service leads, procurement specialists and regulatory supervisors, the course focuses on translating governance expectations into operational decisions and records. Participants practise mapping AI use cases, assessing impacts and supplier evidence, and setting human-review, monitoring and incident-escalation routines using tools such as inventories, risk registers and review checklists.
audienceIntro: This course suits intermediate professionals who shape, procure, supervise or review AI use in public services and regulatory functions. It is designed for people who need to connect governance expectations to operational controls and decision records.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with public administration, regulatory oversight, digital services, AI procurement or data governance is expected. Coding or programming is not required. Advanced AI topics receive conceptual and operational treatment; the course does not require model development.
